how-do-i-document-a-change-order.html.text:
← Construction daily log & evidence pack

How do I document a change order on a job site?

The superintendent points at a wall and says move it. You move it. Six weeks later the invoice comes back queried, the superintendent has moved to another job, and the entire question of whether that was extra work rests on a text message thread and what two people remember about a Tuesday.

The fix is not a better argument later. It is a dated record written the same day.

Open the free daily log & evidence pack

What to capture, the same day

  • Date and time. The single field that turns a note into evidence.
  • Who directed it, and how. Name, role, and whether it was spoken on site, by phone, by text, or on a marked-up drawing.
  • What was directed. In plain words, as instructed — not as you later priced it.
  • What it changed. Work added, work removed, work now out of sequence.
  • What it consumed. Crew, hours, plant, materials, and any standby or delay it caused elsewhere.
  • Site conditions. Weather, access, other trades in the way — the things that are obvious on the day and unprovable afterwards.
  • What is still outstanding. The written confirmation, signature, or drawing revision you have asked for and not yet received.

That last field is the one most often skipped and the most useful. A record that says "requested written confirmation on the 14th, none received" is a fact about the paperwork, and it is far stronger than remembering that you asked.

Contemporaneous beats reconstructed

A log written on the day is a record of observation. The same facts assembled six weeks later from memory, photos and messages is a reconstruction — one made after you knew there was a dispute, and read that way. Nothing you can do afterwards recovers the difference, which is why the few minutes at the end of the day are worth more than the hour spent arguing later.

How the tool helps

  1. Record the day's observable facts — work, conditions, crew, delays, scope changes — in the browser. Nothing is uploaded; there is no account and no server.
  2. Download the dated JSON evidence pack.
  3. Keep your own backup. The pack is your record, and the tool holds nothing for you.
  4. Hand the pack, or a summary from it, to the project manager or customer alongside the change order.

It is deliberately evidence-only: it records what you entered and what still needs review. It does not certify work, decide entitlement, file a claim, or promise payment.

Common questions

How do I document a change order on a job site?

Write it the same day, while the detail is still exact. Record the date and time, who gave the direction and in what form, what was actually directed, what work it added or removed, the crew and hours it consumed, any delay or standby it caused, and what you are still waiting for in writing. A record made on the day is contemporaneous; the same facts assembled six weeks later from memory and text messages are a reconstruction, and they are treated very differently in a dispute.

Why does a daily log matter if I trust the customer?

Most disputes are not about bad faith. They are about two people remembering a busy day differently, months later, after the person who gave the direction has moved to another project. A dated log of observable facts — weather, crew on site, deliveries, access problems, what was directed and by whom — costs a few minutes at the end of the day and removes the need for anyone's memory to be the evidence.

Does this tool file a claim or prove I am owed money?

No. It records what you entered, with dates, and exports it as a portable JSON pack you keep. It does not certify work, determine entitlement, file a claim, or promise payment, and nothing about a record it produces makes a change order approved. Entitlement depends on your contract and the law that governs it; take advice on those.

No warranty. This free page is not legal, contractual, insurance, or engineering advice, and it does not establish entitlement to payment, time, or a variation. It is a record of what you typed. Whether a change order is owed depends on your contract and applicable law — verify with a qualified professional before relying on any record for a claim or a dispute. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the authors accept no liability for loss or damage arising from its use.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free and experimental and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. Export and back up your own records; do not use this as a system of record.

      Common questions
      Does an evidence pack prove a change order or delay claim?
      No. The footer says it outright: evidence, not a compliance or payment guarantee. It gives you a dated, structured JSON record of what you typed on the day; whether that supports a claim still depends on your contract terms and what actually happened on site.
      What do the flags under the evidence pack mean?
      They point out gaps in what you filled in — no crew listed, no site conditions, or a change/delay entry with no requester or no description — so you notice a thin record before it's the only thing you have. They check completeness, not whether what you wrote is accurate.
      Does my log get saved anywhere, or do I need to download it before closing the tab?
      Yes, now: each entry you submit is saved in this browser (local storage), so it is still there next time you open the page in the same browser on the same device. Nothing is uploaded. It's specific to this browser — a different browser, a different device, or clearing site data won't have it — so still download or copy anything you need to keep somewhere else.
      Can I get one record spanning multiple days, not just today?
      Yes. The project log history section lists every entry saved in this browser, filtered to the project name you typed if any. "Download CSV (spreadsheet)" bundles the same saved entries into one spreadsheet-ready file, one row per day, with every field the form collects, for sorting, filtering, or handing to someone who wants a spreadsheet instead of JSON.
      Does anything I type leave my browser?
      No. The log, the change/delay details, the generated evidence pack, and the saved history are all built, stored, and downloaded locally; nothing is uploaded to a server.

vs-procore.html.text:
← Construction Daily Log Evidence Pack

This evidence pack vs. Procore

Two different shapes: Procore is account-based project-management software for running a whole company's projects. This page is a free, private worksheet that turns one site day — or several combined — into a dated evidence record.

What each tool is for

Procore is construction project-management software founded in 2002 and headquartered in Carpinteria, California. It is sold as an ongoing subscription account and covers daily logs, RFIs, submittals, drawings, photos, quality and safety, and financials across a company's whole project portfolio, used by general contractors, owners, and specialty contractors mostly on commercial and larger-scale work. Procore's own pricing page is not reachable from this session to confirm today's exact plan names or dollar figures, so no price for it is invented here: only its well-documented identity and category — account-based, subscription construction project-management software — are stated, and no dollar amount for Procore appears on this page.

This tool does none of what Procore does. It does not manage RFIs or submittals, track drawings, run financials, or store any project record on a server. It takes one site day — crew, weather or site conditions, work completed, and any change or delay, with who requested it and its time or cost impact — flags what is missing before a thin record is all you have, and turns it into a dated JSON evidence pack. Every entry you submit is saved in your own browser, so at the end of a job you can download one combined, multi-day pack instead of hunting a week of separate files. It runs free in any browser, keeps no account, and uploads nothing you type.

QuestionWhere to answer it
I run a contracting company and need RFIs, submittals, drawings, and financials tracked across every project in one system.Procore, or a comparable project-management platform — running a whole company's projects is not something this tool does.
What happened on site today, and is anything missing from the record before it's the only thing I have?This evidence pack — free, private, no account, with completeness flags on each entry.
I need a dated record of several days combined into one file to hand a customer or project manager.This evidence pack's "download combined evidence pack" action across every saved day.
How do I document a change order the same day it happens?This tool's own change-order documentation walkthrough.
Do I need to create an account or sign up to use the tool?This evidence pack: no. Procore is used through a subscription account.
Does the record prove a change order or delay claim, or certify the work?Neither tool does this. It depends on your contract terms and what actually happened on site.

Most contractors get different value from each: Procore (or a comparable platform) for running RFIs, submittals, drawings, and financials across a whole company as an ongoing subscription, and a private tool like this one for a same-day, no-login record of what happened on site, and a combined pack across several days, before or alongside opening a business system. This page's own output is an evidence record of what you typed, not a certification of work, an entitlement determination, or a payment guarantee, and neither this tool nor Procore settles a contract dispute on its own.

This tool needs no account and no sign-in: it is a static page, entries are stored only in your own browser's local storage, and nothing you type is uploaded.

Should I use this evidence pack or Procore?

They do different jobs, and a contractor running real crews may end up touching both. Procore is construction project-management software founded in 2002 and headquartered in Carpinteria, California. It is sold as an ongoing subscription account and covers daily logs, RFIs, submittals, drawings, photos, quality and safety, and financials across a company's whole project portfolio, used by general contractors, owners, and specialty contractors on commercial and larger-scale work. This tool does one narrower thing: it takes what happened on site today — crew, conditions, work completed, and any change or delay — flags gaps before they become a thin record, and turns it into a dated JSON evidence pack you can download the same day, with no account and nothing uploaded.
